kind: controlled interruption and recovery of a business transaction (design v3.2 §11, AP32-17 testnet exercise, AP32-33)
environment: examples/merchant-agent CLI with its durable SQLite execution store (data/agent-v32-20261008.sqlite), buying the check from an isolated local API (127.0.0.1:4043, database data/selftest-v32-20261008.sqlite); project testnet funds only
procedure: 1. `merchant-agent run APPROVED_PAYMENT --crash-after-broadcast`: order created by the order-creator role, check fee paid, report delivered, decision NO_POLICY_VIOLATION, final validation PASS, business transaction signed, persisted (SIGNED), broadcast marker written with the head block, raw bytes sent — then the process ended with exit code 137 before any receipt was awaited
2. store state right after the crash: BROADCAST_ATTEMPTED, business_status empty, broadcast_block 66097023, tx 0x66ef771c…95dd09, nonce 13

3. next CLI invocation: reconciliation from the store ran first and closed the attempt from the original hash and the order state — CONFIRMED / SUCCESS at block 66097032, note 'reconciled from the original transaction hash and the order state'; nothing was re-signed
4. independent read of the original transaction's receipt from the testnet RPC: status 0x1, block 66097032, from the demo-runner, 2 logs
finding: the rehearsal script expected the next `run` to be refused while the attempt was unresolved; the transaction had already confirmed (~9 s), so reconciliation closed it and that same `run` invocation then proceeded to a second, unrelated purchase (attempt 235486c1, nonce 14). The CLI was changed the same day: when the store holds open attempts, `run` reconciles them and exits (code 3) without starting a purchase; a new purchase needs its own explicit command after the old outcome has been seen
notInjected: no crash between the broadcast marker and the send (that window rests on the runner/API fault-injection tests), no dropped-transaction rebroadcast, no same-nonce replacement; those paths are covered by unit tests against a fake chain
